name: Red Sea, Yemen and Saudi Arabia
label: CRITICAL
key_judgment: Houthi missile and drone fire on Saudi Arabia will very likely continue at its current tempo, with the reopened Riyadh airport and the Yanbu-Rabigh export corridor the most probable targets; that corridor now carries Saudi crude rerouted away from Hormuz.
basis: Since 6 November: the coalition said it destroyed a Houthi cruise missile aimed at the Riyadh region on 7 November (party claim, I-978). The level holds on the continued Houthi launch tempo. Since 5 November: the coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles toward Najran and a drone over Makkah on 6 November, with debris at Najran and no confirmed damage; the Houthi spokesman denied the coalition's 5 November Madinah intercept. Both are party claims and the level holds on continued fire. Since 5 November: the coalition said it destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward the Medina region after Saudi civil defence alerted Yanbu Governorate (party claim). Since 3 November: the Houthis claimed drone and ballistic missile attacks on an airport and an airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia on 4 November; the coalition said it intercepted three drones (Mecca region, Eastern Province, south) and Saudi Civil Defence stood down an alert in Jazan. Since 27 October: the coalition reports interceptions of Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Province (29 Oct) and the southern region (1 Nov); Saudi Civil Defence reports one person wounded by shrapnel in Riyadh; Houthi claims of six attacks on Saudi oil and airport targets (30 Oct) lack independent corroboration. No Saudi-confirmed hit on energy infrastructure has been found since 21 October; the level holds on continued fire at Riyadh and the Eastern Province and the role of the Yanbu-Rabigh corridor. The coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province and four drones aimed at the south early on 27 October, after intercepting a Riyadh-bound missile on 26 October and saying it destroyed four launchers, five missile storage tunnels and a depot in Houthi territory. The Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid airport and oil pumping stations on 26 October; Riyadh has not confirmed either. Egypt's parliament authorised Sisi on 26 October, by a two-thirds vote, to support Saudi Arabia defensively, and a Houthi political bureau member called this a declaration of war on Yemen on 27 October. Israeli media, relayed by CTP-ISW, report an unverified $1 billion Saudi offer to the Houthis under an Iran-brokered deal. INTERTANKO notes no Houthi maritime operations for some time. Carrier suspensions run to mid-November for most European and Gulf airlines and to January 2027 for Cathay Pacific.
sponsor_posture: Houthis act with Iranian backing; Saudi Arabia and its coalition retaliate in Yemen.
cyber_nexus: Pro-Iran hacktivist personas target Gulf financial and government sites; Unit 42 reports Saudi ERP credential phishing and utility-bill scams. Egypt's authorisation of defensive support could add Egyptian banks and government portals to these personas' target set.
scenario: A Houthi strike closes Riyadh's airport for days during a regional leadership meeting, stranding staff, while phishing lures impersonate Saudi utility and payment portals.
so_what: Travel and staff safety in Saudi Arabia, Red Sea and Suez shipping insurance, and a second chokepoint on Gulf energy exports.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further Houthi salvos on Riyadh, the Eastern Province, the southern provinces and the East-West Pipeline corridor are very likely, with coalition strikes on Sanaa and the Red Sea coast continuing. Next 30 days: sustained pressure on Saudi airports and western export infrastructure is likely; an Egyptian deployment would likely stay defensive and limited, and Houthi action against Red Sea and Suez traffic in response to Egypt's move remains unlikely. The Tehran channel and the reported Saudi offer give a narrow route to restraint; carrier suspensions will likely run through November.

name: Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf
label: CRITICAL
key_judgment: Iran will very likely keep the strait effectively closed to unescorted traffic while the post-midterm US decision on a large strike is open: the Guards claimed four more tankers destroyed by mines on 4 November, Trump said the US must do 'something large', and the WSJ reports he has not decided, so a US strike package in the coming week is a live alternative unless the Qatari reopening sequence is agreed.
basis: Since 6 November: gCaptain reported one seafarer killed in a suspected missile attack on the tanker Velos Sapphire, and Iran's navy claimed a further mine strike on a tanker east of the strait, which no maritime authority has confirmed. The Straits Live brief shows the strait as closed, though it records conflicting reports of a reopening, with about 132 vessels holding and Brent near $98. Attacks on shipping continue and the level holds. Since 4 November: UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash-Shamal, Qatar; the Guards and the Iranian army said at least five tankers and a tugboat hit mines on 5 November (unverified, counts differ); unnamed Pentagon officials told The New York Times US forces are poised to resume major combat operations, with no decision confirmed. Qatar's mediation continues and the level holds. On 3 and 4 November: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles in the engine room 14 nautical miles northeast of Limah off Oman, with no casualties; Brent fell 8.6% to $94.66 on 4 November, its lowest since 4 September, as traders priced de-escalation after the US midterms, while an unnamed senior Iranian official dismissed reports of progress in talks. Attacks on shipping continue, so the level holds. Since 3 November: the Guards said four 'non-compliant' tankers were destroyed by mines south of the strait and two vessels halted (Iranian claim, unverified); Trump told Fox News the US must do 'something large', possibly a 'heavy hit', and called the Qeshm strike a 'minor attack' on an anti-aircraft facility; the WSJ reports he leans toward a large attack after the midterms but has not decided. Since 2 November: UKMTO reported 30 attacks on commercial vessels in the region in October, a record; a vessel was hit off Oman on 1 November and an India-flagged cargo vessel off Oman on 3 November, killing one crew member; US officials said US forces struck Iranian targets on Qeshm after the Guards fired on a US aircraft, while Iran's navy and IRIB claim mine and fire incidents that remain unverified. Since 27 October: UKMTO reported another tanker struck by an unknown projectile on exit from the strait (29 Oct); Araghchi said Qatari mediators asked Iran to compress its sequence to two days, with reopening on the second day, though no agreement exists; Brent fell to $109.23 on 2 Nov. The 1 November PGSA deadline for Sinokor passed without an enforcement report found. UKMTO verified on 26 October that an outbound tanker was disabled by a projectile in the strait on 23 October, the day after the Limah LPG strike, and on 26 October logged a vessel on fire 63 nm southeast of Al-Faw as suspicious activity. JMIC holds Hormuz at Severe and the wider Gulf at Substantial, citing five attacks inside the Gulf since 7 October. INTERTANKO counts more than 30 US-facilitated transits a day, about 90% tankers, against a pre-war baseline near 138, finds no credible evidence for Iranian mine claims and expects conditions to hold until the midterms. Iran's strait authority said on 27 October it will act against all Sinokor tankers, which carried nearly 40% of Hormuz crude last month, from 1 November. In Tehran, Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys agreed on 26 October to continue talks; Iran lists seven US conditions and Qatari mediators are pursuing a five-day exchange of reopening for a blockade lift. DNI Clayton warned Iran is in advanced stages of planning attacks on US regional targets. Brent settled at $115.81 on 26 October and traded at $114.70 on 27 October.
sponsor_posture: Iran (IRGC Navy) is the principal; Tehran frames shipping attacks as leverage over US politics. The US holds the blockade; US officials said US forces struck Iranian targets on Qeshm on 2 November after the Guards fired on a US aircraft, and Washington had earlier pledged no strike on Iran before 3 November.
cyber_nexus: IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers moved from Unitronics to Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers; Iran-linked intrusions hit US water utilities in 12+ states from late July; a UK power plant was shut for four days; about 60 hacktivist groups run DDoS and defacement. No new observed Iran-linked intrusion against US infrastructure was found for 25-27 October.
scenario: An IRGC-aligned persona claims a DDoS and data-leak operation against a US or Gulf payments brand during a spike in tanker attacks, while a separate actor probes internet-exposed OT at a facilities vendor.
so_what: Energy-cost and FX shock, Gulf staff and data-center continuity, and a higher chance of Iranian cyber activity against US financial and payment brands within days of kinetic events.
outlook: Next 72 hours: a US decision on a strike package and Qatari feedback on the two-day sequence are the main variables; further tanker incidents and Iranian claims of mine strikes are likely. Next 30 days (unchanged from the prior review): a strike package stays on the table unless a transit bargain is reached; enforcement against Sinokor tankers would likely cut escorted crude flows.

name: Afghanistan and Pakistan border
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Pakistan-Taliban border clashes and TTP-linked attacks inside Pakistan will likely continue; the failure of the Moscow talks removes the nearest diplomatic off-ramp.
basis: Since 5 November: Pakistani security sources claim a TTP infiltration attempt was foiled in Kurram and Taliban posts were heavily damaged after Taliban fire; no casualties were reported and the Taliban have not replied. The level holds. Since 27 October: Pakistani security sources claim strikes on Taliban posts after border firing (30 Oct); the Taliban account and independent confirmation are missing. ISPR says six TTP militants and two soldiers were killed in Dera Ismail Khan's Zarkani area on 24 October. Pakistan's Foreign Office on 26 October rejected the Taliban's claim of 1,119 civilian casualties since 2022 and reaffirmed its right to self-defence, after a minister warned of all necessary measures if Afghan soil is used for attacks. On 25 October KP Governor Kundi confirmed the chief minister and speaker are under house arrest and said the 11 October emergency may run beyond six months; on 27 October a 48-member council was tasked with persuading militants to leave the 12 emergency districts through jirgas. The Taliban interior ministry on 27 October blamed Pakistan for drug smuggling. No new Kurram-Paktia exchange or mass-casualty attack was found between 18 and 27 October.
sponsor_posture: Pakistan's military; the Afghan Taliban; TTP and the IMP alliance.
scenario: A suicide attack on a Pakistani city disrupts staff travel and a regional processing center.
so_what: Staff safety in Pakistan; regional travel.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further ISPR-announced operations in southern KP and South Waziristan are likely, with TTP retaliation against police probable. Next 30 days: Islamabad's explicit warning of further action raises the likelihood of renewed Pakistani strikes into Afghanistan and Taliban border fire, with no diplomatic channel active.

name: Horn of Africa
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Ethiopia's federal offensive may be shifting toward a protracted counter-insurgency, a realistic possibility, as the TDF reoccupies vacated areas such as Rama and reportedly Abergele; an Ethiopia-Eritrea interstate war remains a realistic possibility while the border stays contested, and the 4 November Ethiopia-Sudan consular expulsions reportedly add a second interstate axis, per unnamed officials.
basis: Since 4 November: Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomats out and Sudan closed Ethiopia's Gedaref consulate, per unnamed officials; the TPLF claims 500 federal soldiers killed near Aksum (unverified). The level holds. Since 2 November: ACLED records the ENDF entering Sheraro on 3 November and a drone strike believed to be by the ENDF that killed 12 civilians in Rama on 30 October; the WHO chief says the violence is pushing the northern health system closer to collapse. No Somalia reporting newer than 27 October was found. Since 27 October: drone strikes on the Jaari 2 displacement camp in Amhara killed at least 15 on 30 October per rescue sources cited by Reuters. No independently reported Tigray front-line change since the 22 October federal capture of Abiy Addi and Zana; TPF sources claim federal troops captured TPLF commander John Medid in Central Tigray on 26 October (unverified). On 25 October the ENDF chief of staff accused Eritrea and Egypt of backing the TPLF and claimed seizure of an arms shipment via Massawa, sustaining interstate rhetoric. In Somalia, Reuters reports dozens of soldiers killed in an al-Shabaab battle in Buurhakaba district around 26 October (al-Shabaab claims 321), while Laftagareen forces fought the army outside Baidoa and the Burhakabo push stalled at Leego. The Orthodox Synod reports more than 60 Christians killed in Arsi, Oromia, on 20 and 24 October.
sponsor_posture: Ethiopia; Eritrea and Egypt (accused by Addis of backing rebels); Somalia neutral.
scenario: Ethiopian strikes on Eritrean ports disrupt Red Sea traffic already diverted by the Hormuz closure.
so_what: Red Sea shipping, East African operations and staff; heightened risk to staff movement around Baidoa and Mogadishu approaches.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued clashes in central and southern Tigray and further drone strikes; al-Shabaab and Laftagareen forces likely keep harassing the stalled federal column in Bay. Next 30 days: the Tigray war may shift to insurgency while Eritrean and Ethiopian rhetoric keeps interstate-war risk alive; the convergence of clan rebellion and al-Shabaab in Bay and Hiran likely erodes Mogadishu's southern positions.

name: Israel, Lebanon and Syria
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Israel-Hezbollah hostilities will likely continue at their current level through Israel's 27 October election, with a sharp escalation likely only if Hezbollah joins an Iranian attack.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Reassessed 2 November: no new reporting found for 27 October to 2 November; the level holds. On 26 October, the eve of the election, Israel struck between Qantara and Bani Hayyan, carried out two major demolitions in Zawtar Sharqieh and shelled about a dozen south Lebanon localities, with one person hurt by unexploded ordnance; no Hezbollah fire into Israel was reported. Hezbollah signals are mixed: a senior official told al-Liwaa on 26 October the group has given no guarantee it will stay out of a war on Iran, while MP Fadlallah said Iran has not asked it to fight. Lebanese security sources told Reuters Iran has sent tens of millions of dollars for Hezbollah's military reconstitution. Voting opened on 27 October with 31.5% turnout at noon, the highest at that hour since 1973; the elections committee found no systematic tampering and Katz urged voters to back Netanyahu to finish the job in Iran. Check Point reports attacks on Israeli organisations up 55% year on year, with Handala tying its leaks to the vote and groups discussing election-day DoS against the Bank of Israel and ministries.
sponsor_posture: Iran backs Hezbollah; Israel's posture hardens before its election.
cyber_nexus: Handala (MOIS-linked) ties its leak operations to the Israeli election; Check Point counts about 2,700 attacks a week on Israeli organisations, with election-day DoS discussed against the Bank of Israel.
scenario: A Hezbollah decision to join an Iranian strike triggers Israeli strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs and a regional flight shutdown.
so_what: Staff and vendor exposure in Israel and Lebanon; Israeli technology suppliers as targets of Iranian data-leak operations.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued Israeli strikes and demolitions in south Lebanon and incursions in Quneitra through the count and its immediate aftermath, with hacktivist DoS and Handala leak claims likely to continue around the results. Next 30 days: coalition bargaining after the vote is unlikely to change Israel's posture in Lebanon or Syria; the main escalation path runs through a post-midterm US or Israeli strike on Iran, where Hezbollah's ambiguous position and Iranian-funded reconstitution raise the chance it joins.

name: Russia and Ukraine
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Reciprocal energy-infrastructure attacks will very likely continue into the winter: Russia's 3 November raid (289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles, per Zelenskiy) knocked three of DTEK's five thermal plants offline and cut power in Kyiv and at least six regions, hours after Washington announced trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November, and no energy truce is confirmed by either side.
basis: Since 6 November: ISW counted 227 Russian drones overnight into 6 November (86 jet-powered) with new outages reported by Ukrenergo, and geolocated footage of a smoke plume at the Afipsky refinery, at least the sixth strike on it this year. The reciprocal pattern continues and the level holds. Since 5 November: Ukraine's General Staff reported 196 Russian drones shot down or jammed overnight into 6 November with outages in seven regions including Kyiv and Kharkiv, and Russia says it intercepted 142 Ukrainian drones while a fire hit the Afipsky refinery (both party claims). The level holds. Since 4 November: Russia launched 310 long-range drones overnight, 272 intercepted per the Air Force; six were killed and 50 injured over the past day, and energy sites were hit in six regions with emergency outages in Kyiv and other regions (Kyiv Independent). Since 2 November: Russia struck a shelter and aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 31 by Ukrainian count; the 3 November raid hit energy and rail targets from Odesa to Rivne (Zelenskiy's figures, Reuters), and Russian officials say Ukraine set a Yaroslavl refinery on fire. Witkoff said delegations meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. Since 27 October: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia sent 193 strike drones overnight into 2 November, below the 500-drone threshold; Ukrainian drones reportedly hit three Russian refineries between 30 October and 1 November, with a Russian governor confirming a damaging attack in Kstovo district. Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones overnight into 27 October, mainly at Kyiv, killing one, closing the Pivdennyi Bridge and disrupting the Green metro line; Zelensky says most targets were energy, logistics and urban infrastructure. A drone cut power to part of Chernivtsi on 26 October and Ukrenergo reported outages in six regions. Zelensky says Ukraine received 24 US Patriot interceptors in 90 days. Ukrainian drones killed two in Bryansk and one on a bus in occupied Zaporizhzhia on 27 October; the General Staff claims hits on the Energiya (Yelets) and Proton-Electrotex (Oryol) microelectronics plants. Russia claims a strike on a cargo ship bound for Chornomorsk. The Oleshky local ceasefire began on 27 October, while Peskov says talks imply no limits on military operations.
sponsor_posture: Russia escalates against Ukraine's grid; Ukraine targets Russian fuel revenue. US-Ukraine relations are strained.
cyber_nexus: Sandworm-class operators have a long record against Ukrainian energy; pro-Russian DDoS crews (NoName057(16)) target European governments and banks.
scenario: A wiper hits a Ukrainian distribution operator during a cold snap and spreads to a European subsidiary through a shared IT provider.
so_what: European energy prices, sanctions-compliance load, and DDoS against European financial sites.
outlook: Next 72 hours: continued Russian raids on generation, substations and rail, and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. Next 30 days: the Abu Dhabi round on 10 and 11 November, where an energy truce is Kyiv's priority; Trump's earlier truce announcements were not confirmed by either side. A strike disabling a major Russian export terminal would argue for CRITICAL.

name: Sahel and West Africa
label: HIGH
key_judgment: JNIM will likely keep pressure on central Mali garrisons and Bamako's fuel supply, while its war with Islamic State Sahel Province spreads toward Niger and Nigeria; the army's return to Kidal does not reduce pressure in the centre.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Reassessed 2 November: no new reporting found for 27 October to 2 November; the level holds. No new major attack in Mali, Burkina Faso or Niger was found for 25-27 October; the latest confirmed events remain the 18-19 October IS Sahel massacre near Menaka (54 bodies found at Tagadayat, per the army on 24 October) and Niger's 25 October overnight petrol-sales ban. In Nigeria, the toll from the 23 October raid on Binnari, Taraba State, rose to at least 62 dead (AP, NEMA). Goïta is due at the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on 28-29 October. No new reporting on the Bamako fuel blockade or attacks on Bamako.
sponsor_posture: JNIM (al-Qaeda); FLA separatists; Russian Africa Corps supports the junta.
scenario: A renewed blockade of Bamako forces evacuation of regional staff and suspends payment-network services in Mali.
so_what: Staff and agent networks in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger.
outlook: Next 72 hours: Moscow summit announcements on Russian security support to the AES are likely; further army strikes around Menaka and possible ISSP reprisals. Next 30 days: JNIM-ISSP fighting in the tri-border area and attacks in northern Nigeria likely continue; regional fuel stress in Mali and Niger bears watching.

name: Sudan
label: HIGH
key_judgment: Sudan's war will likely intensify over the next 30 days without talks, with mass-casualty drone strikes on towns, attacks on power and water infrastructure, and growing spillover into Abyei and Chad.
basis: Since 3 November: the RSF and SPLM-N claim the Sali base in Blue Nile and the army says its air defences downed a drone that crossed from Ethiopia (party claims); Ethiopia and Sudan expelled diplomats and closed a consulate on 4 November. The level holds. Since 2 November: Sudan filed complaints against Ethiopia at the UN Security Council and the AU over a tally of 70 drone assaults (government figures, unverified); Sudan Tribune reports a suspected RSF drone strike on a fuel station in South Kordofan that killed at least seven. Since 27 October: drone strikes hit substations at New Halfa, Aroma and al-Ghazali (2 Nov) with 18 strikes on the grid reported in a week and 15 substations counted since early October; the army blames Ethiopia, a claim Al Jazeera presents as the government's and could not verify. A day after the 26 October coordinated RSF drone strikes on power stations in Al-Jazira, Gedaref, White Nile and Sennar, a drone hit the Al-Markhiyat transformer station in Khartoum early on 27 October, cutting power across much of Khartoum and Al-Jazira (AFP; electricity company source blames the RSF). A drone strike on a Nyala market on the evening of 26 October killed 21 people, a hospital medic told AFP, which did not attribute it; army sources claim strikes that night destroyed RSF command sites and air defences near Nyala airport. On 26 October the foreign ministry rejected famine warnings from 32 countries and argued a truce would let the RSF regroup. No talks are in view.
sponsor_posture: SAF (backed by Egypt); RSF (external backing alleged).
scenario: Sustained drone strikes on Khartoum and eastern substations knock out power and telecoms, cutting payment acceptance and correspondent-banking connectivity in army-held Sudan.
so_what: Humanitarian payments and sanctions screening; regional staff.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further RSF drone strikes on grid and fuel sites in Khartoum and army-held states, and continued army strikes on Nyala, Ed Daein and El Fasher. Next 30 days: infrastructure attacks likely widen outages in the capital and the east, while the Abyei dispute and Chad border strikes sustain spillover risk.

name: Europe: hybrid threats and sabotage
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: Russian-directed sabotage will likely keep targeting the Starlink and space-ground network supporting Ukraine, alongside defence-industrial and logistics sites, below the Article 5 threshold, while Iranian intelligence will likely keep plotting against Jewish communities and, on UK police assessment, US-used military sites in Europe.
basis: Reassessed 7 November: ISW reported hoax bomb threats to at least 18 flights and airports on 6 November and more than 50 that week, with no attribution and no explosives found. ISW ties the campaign to Kremlin objectives without naming an actor, so it stays a watch item pending attribution and the level holds. Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Since 27 October: a Brasov arson suspect was detained in Warsaw (28 Oct) and two Germans were arrested over the Starlink antenna fire near Sofia (23 Oct); Bulgaria says it has no direct evidence linking the October Black Sea drone attacks to Moscow, with 21 people missing. Romania's SRI and DIICOT said on 26 October that a Russia-coordinated network of two Belarusians and a Ukrainian set the 14 September fire beside ROMARM's Carfil plant in Brasov; two have been arrested and were allegedly preparing similar attacks in Germany, and a warrant was issued for the third, believed to be in Poland. A European Parliamentary Research Service briefing (26 October) records Russia-linked cyber activity in nine member states, including Cyprus and Polish heat and power plants. Sikorski attributed the hybrid campaign to a GRU unit on 26 October; Moscow promised a tough response to Moldova's expulsion of a Russian diplomat; no new Black Sea ship strike off Romania or Bulgaria was found for 25-27 October.
sponsor_posture: Russia (GRU-directed proxies, often recruited online); Iran (criminal proxies).
cyber_nexus: NoName057(16) pays volunteers in crypto for DDoS; hacktivist DDoS follows political events within days.
scenario: A recruited proxy sets fire to a logistics hub that hosts a payments data-center cage, while a DDoS wave hits the same country's banks.
so_what: Physical security at European data and logistics sites, executive protection, and DDoS readiness for European services.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further drone strikes on merchant shipping in the western Black Sea, a possible Russian retaliatory step against Moldova, and further detail on the Brasov network's other attacks. Next 30 days: the Bulgarian runoff on 1 November, attacks or arrests linked to Starlink ground stations and defence suppliers, and pro-Russian DDoS; a third fatal strike in Romanian waters or an armed drone crossing into NATO territory would argue for HIGH.

name: Korean Peninsula and DPRK revenue operations
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: DPRK pressure is rising on two fronts: a cluster-bomb warhead test on 31 October and the FBI's attribution of the roughly $6.36 billion Binance theft to TraderTraitor; revenue operations remain the most direct state threat to financial firms, while a border incident is the main near-term military risk.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Since 3 November: South Korea's JCS reported several missiles fired from Sondok on 4 November, the fourth launch in a month, and Pyongyang rejected the FBI's Binance attribution; Binance's incident report describes a campaign from June through 29 October that ran through fake recruiter interviews. Since 27 October: North Korea fired a tactical ballistic missile with a cluster-bomb warhead on 31 October; the FBI attributes the roughly $6.36 billion Binance theft of about 29 October to TraderTraitor, with TRM Labs and Chainalysis concurring. The level holds at ELEVATED because the rubric reserves HIGH for active hostilities, and the theft is a financial operation without sustained hostilities. On 26-27 October Reuters, SBS and NK News observed North Korean 122mm self-propelled howitzers at two western border locations opposite Gimpo, with fortification work continuing; on 27 October South Korea's JCS assessed them as legacy artillery deployed in plain view and said they cannot be considered the new tactical weapons Kim Yo Jong threatened. Deepfakes exaggerating the deployment circulated widely the same week. KCNA reported a DPRK letter to the UN Security Council warning of self-defence measures. Switzerland's foreign minister is due in Pyongyang from 29 October to open a political office. OFAC delisted three SEK Studio-linked Chinese parties on 21 October without explanation. Loudspeaker activation had not been reported through 27 October.
sponsor_posture: DPRK (RGB); revenue crime runs as statecraft.
cyber_nexus: APT38 / Lazarus target exchanges, bridges and banks; IT workers recruited through third-country fronts.
scenario: A remote engineer hired through a staffing vendor, fronted by a third-country 'interview associate', exfiltrates source code and API keys for a payments platform.
so_what: Hiring and contractor identity proofing, crypto and settlement infrastructure, and sanctions exposure from DPRK payments.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further missile or warhead tests are likely after five launch days in October, and a border incident remains the main military risk. Next 30 days: laundering of Binance proceeds, with the FBI's 628 published addresses as the lead, and PHP2Shell exploitation remain the financial-sector cyber risk.

name: Mexico and the US cartel campaign
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: US military pressure on cartels will likely widen from maritime strikes to land targets in Latin America within months, raising retaliation risk and sanctions-screening load in Mexico.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Since 27 October: the trucker blockades ended within 34 hours with the toll-deduction cap unresolved; no new US strike or armed-drone item was found. Sheinbaum answered the NYT-reported US memo on 26 October, saying Mexico coordinates with Washington but will not accept US forces on its territory and that such requests have recurred under Trump. No new US boat strike was found after the 4 October Caribbean strike, and OFAC listed no cartel designations through 26 October. Mexican forces arrested Los Rusos operator 'El Isra' in Mexicali on 26 October; Noroeste counted 42 violent deaths in Sinaloa in the week to 25 October, 5% below the prior week. A Canacar-led national trucker strike on 26 October over highway insecurity and extortion blocked several federal highways without a deal.
sponsor_posture: US military and Treasury; Mexican cartels designated as FTOs in February 2025.
cyber_nexus: Cartels use drones for surveillance and attack; financial networks span racing, construction, trucking and fuel.
scenario: A US strike on a cartel facility triggers retaliation against foreign businesses in Sinaloa, and OFAC adds front companies that appear in merchant portfolios.
so_what: Merchant and correspondent-bank sanctions screening in Mexico; staff safety in Sinaloa and Tamaulipas; road-freight disruption and cargo-security exposure for clients with Mexican supply chains while the trucker strike lasts.
outlook: Next 72 hours: whether the trucker strike persists and how Washington responds to Sheinbaum's public refusal. Next 30 days: pre-midterm pressure (3 November) raises the odds of a resumed boat strike, a first land action or new OFAC designations.

name: South China Sea and Luzon Strait
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: China-Philippines friction will likely continue at sea, with the next Sierra Madre rotation the most probable flashpoint; the ASEAN summit in Manila and APEC diplomacy argue for restraint over the next three weeks.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Since 27 October: China downgraded its ADMM-Plus delegation and accused Manila of obstruction; no at-sea incident was found. The AFP counted 54 Chinese vessels at West Philippine Sea features for 20-26 October, up from 31 the prior week, excluding the PLAN Liaoning group that Trinidad said passed within 15 miles of Philippine landmass before exiting south (27 Oct). On 25 October the PCG expelled a foreign fishing vessel from Pag-asa's territorial sea while CCG 21581 and two RHIBs trailed it, without interference. The DFA on 26 October denied any subsea-cable arrangement with Taiwan, walking back a diplomat's Bashi Channel remarks. Manila hosts the ADMM and ADMM-Plus in Cebu on 28-29 October with Hegseth expected; China's attendance is unconfirmed and its foreign ministry warned on 26 October against attempts to 'hijack ASEAN'. No ramming, water-cannon or Sierra Madre incident was found for 24-27 October.
sponsor_posture: PRC (CCG, maritime militia, PLA Southern Theater Command).
cyber_nexus: Chinese state groups run espionage against Philippine and Southeast Asian government networks (the 8 October multinational advisory on Integrity Technology Group cited Southeast Asian email theft); no new Philippine-specific cyber item found for 24-27 October.
scenario: A collision at Second Thomas Shoal kills a Filipino sailor, invoking the US-Philippines treaty and disrupting shipping through the Luzon Strait.
so_what: Undersea-cable and shipping routes through the Luzon Strait; Manila operations centers.
outlook: Next 72 hours: the ADMM-Plus in Cebu (28-29 October) and a Hegseth-Teodoro bilateral are the focal events; Chinese criticism of US-Philippine statements there is likely, and a CCG show of presence at Scarborough or Second Thomas is possible. Next 30 days: the ASEAN summit in Manila (15-17 November) and Marcos's APEC trip to China argue for restraint, with the next Sierra Madre rotation the most likely flashpoint.

name: Taiwan Strait
label: ELEVATED
key_judgment: PLA pressure on Taiwan will likely stay below blockade over the next 30 days, but CCG jurisdiction claims at Pratas are the most probable route to a boarding or inspection precedent; a named joint exercise remains the warning sign of a step change.
basis: Reassessed 6 November: no new reporting found for 3 to 6 November; the level holds. Since 31 October: a China Coast Guard ship came within 1 nautical mile of a Taiwanese vessel near Pratas, the 13th intrusion this year, and Beijing says it will intensify patrols in waters it calls its jurisdiction; no named PLA exercise was found. Reassessed 2 November: no new reporting found for 27 October to 2 November; the level holds. Taiwan MND detected 3 PLA aircraft sorties (1 across the median line), 6 PLAN ships and 9 official ships in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 26 October, the first aircraft after four days without any during Typhoon Champi; the 27 October report was not yet posted at review time. The CGA said on 24 October that China is pairing maritime militia boats with coast guard ships for 'battlefield preparation' around Taiwan and into the western Pacific, with activity up since June. The PLA Eastern Theater Command marked Beijing's 25 October Taiwan Recovery Day with a propaganda poster and no exercise. A national-security source said on 27 October that Beijing is pressuring entertainers and firms linked to Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen. No named exercise and no new CCG incident at Pratas, Kinmen or Penghu was found for 24-27 October.
sponsor_posture: PRC (PLA Eastern Theater Command, China Coast Guard).
cyber_nexus: Flax Typhoon infrastructure seized by the US; Salt Typhoon remains inside telecom carriers; The Gentlemen hit a Taiwanese manufacturer.
scenario: A named PLA exercise announces inspection zones east of Taiwan; shipping and air routes divert; Taiwan-based semiconductor suppliers delay deliveries.
so_what: Semiconductor supply chain, Asia-Pacific routing of traffic and staff, and Chinese espionage against telecom-dependent authentication.
outlook: Next 72 hours: sortie counts likely return toward pre-typhoon levels of 10 to 30 a day, with CCG patrols resuming around Pratas. Next 30 days: watch for a named exercise and intensified influence and cyber operations ahead of Taiwan's late-November local elections, and further CCG jurisdiction claims around Pratas and Penghu.

name: Venezuela and the Caribbean
label: GUARDED

outlook: Next 72 hours: Machado's first tour stops and any detentions of Vente organisers; watch whether Washington and Machado narrow or widen their public gap on timing. Next 30 days: the fourth round of talks on 11-15 November and the election date remain the pressure points.
